name: wg-classify
_doc: T0 work: classification, routing, tagging, extraction, short operational text.
One route per task class (wg-sn4). Callers address it as model 'dynamic/wg-classify'
and never name a model, which is the point: changing what runs T0 is a change to
this file, not to every caller.
Shape: a cost ceiling keyed on the calling cell, then llama-3.3-70b, falling back
to gemma-4-26b if it fails or times out. Both are Workers AI, so neither needs a
llama first because it was measured first: on classifying fifteen real bead titles
it scored 13/15 at 35.6 neurons and 11.7s, against gemma's 9/15 at 110.8 neurons
and 58.7s (ADR-0018). Gemma is the fallback rather than the default for the same
reason it is the T1 default — it deliberates, which is wasted on work that has one
The budget node is a ceiling, not the budget. wg-budget refuses a dispatch before
an agent starts; this catches control-plane inference, which no bead governs.

Both model elements name a fallback even though the last one has nowhere to fall back to. The documentation calls fallback optional; the API refuses a model element without one, with `Required` at body.elements[3].outputs.fallback. So the terminal model points at end for both outputs, which reads oddly and is what the API accepts.
